note: Probed 2026-08-16 from data/research/arcgis-register-sweep.json's seven Montreal hits. The sweep joins an ArcGIS item to a city by its published EXTENT, which is a lead and not a location, exactly as its own note warns. Two of the seven turned out to be the same 322-tree layer for Otterburn Park, 27 km southeast on the Richelieu, with not one point inside 25 km of Montreal. One is a full public tree inventory, which the semantic-filter rule excludes on principle. What survived is below.

usable.licence: NOT VERIFIED. No licence statement found on the item. Nothing may be imported from it until one is found and quoted in OPEN_DATA_SURVEY.md; until then these are search leads for a research pass, not register entries.
usable.fields: OBJECTID, Espece only. No name, no age, no girth, no condition.
usable.where: All six sit within 800 m of each other on the Mount Royal slope, about 3 km from the city centre, which is the Mount Royal cemetery ground. That is a walkable cluster and the reason this is worth a pass at all.

trees.species_fr_en: Pin noir d'Autriche | European Black Pine

rejected.title: Arbres_remarquables_OP2016 and APP_OP_MilieuxNaturels_WFL1 layer 6 (owner Ariane_CNMSH)
rejected.why_not_montreal: Every one of the 322 records carries MUNICIPALI = 'Otterburn Park'. Nearest point to Montreal centre is 27 km. The extent matched Montreal; the data does not.
rejected.keep_because: This is a genuinely rich register and it carries the field this whole project is short of: DHS_CM, diameter at breast height, on every tree, plus Espece_OK, ETAT (condition), RUE, Description, Habitat and Note. 92 of our published trees have no age and only 13 carry a girth, so a source with a measured diameter on all 322 is worth remembering the day Monteregie or Mont-Saint-Hilaire comes up the queue. Licence unverified, same as above.

rejected.title: Arbres publics (owner stce_02), Inventaire des arbres publics de Saint Lambert, Plantations - Verdissement
rejected.why_not: Full municipal street-tree inventories. Never bulk imported: the register layer takes only what a register itself designates as remarkable.
